chapter: Sidney Bechet and the Paris festival
title: Bechet's $200 gift and how Moore got to the Paris festival
summary: Bechet gave Moore $200 for no reason; when Pete Johnson could not go to Paris, Bechet recommended Moore.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, you mentioned something about going to Paris.
Well, here's what happened. I heard of this International Festival of Jazz and I had no inkling I was going to go. I knew Bechet was going to go because he's been in Europe before. So I
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

remember just the one time Bechet came back, Sidney Bechet is the only man that ever gave me money just because I'm Big Chief. He had just come home from Paris and asked me to come over to his hotel. So I went over to his hotel and there he was sitting on the bed, he's got a pile of bread, a lot of money there, counting his bread. So he came to like two $100 bills, gave me $200, "Here, Chief, this is for you need that." you." I said, "Come on, Sidney, that's your bread. "If you don't take it I'm going to throw it out of the window." I said, "If you throw it through the window, I'm going to be by the window catching it." So I took the $200 and he was glad to give it to me. He's the only one man who ever did that, Sidney Bechet, just because I was Chief. He's incredible.

To go back to the story of how I got to Paris. Nichole Barclay and Eddie Barclay -- it was Nichole that came over here to recruit the musicians that are to appear at this Festival of Jazz. So there was Charlie Parker, Sidney Bechet, Hot Lips Page, some of the boppers that were there, I'll think of them later. I'm recounting the circumstances of how I got to Paris. They got everybody that they wanted to get to appear at the festival in Paris, except one.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Pete Johnson, the boogie-woogie pianist. Pete Johnson couldn't go, he couldn't get out of his contracts up in Albany, New York, and so Nichol heard the conversation because I was on the bandstand and Sidney was on the bandstand, we were getting ready to play our set, and Nichol said, 'Pete Johnson can't go. I have an extra ticket. Do you know anyone . . .' (end of Side 1)

So Nichole asked Sidney, 'Do you know of anybody that we could take, I got an extra ticket, that would leave an impression in Parisian audiences?' And he pointed right straight to me, 'Take him, he'll account for himself.' That's what Sidney Bechet told Nichole Barclay. And so I said, 'Okay.' 'Here's his ticket.'

So we played the set and after the set he wanted to talk to me and we discussed -- and here's what Sidney said, 'Chief, I don't know how much money they're going to give you, but take the job because when you go to Europe you'll be stamped -- you'll gain a lot of prestige going to Europe, especially Paris. That way I got to Paris and I have Sidney Bechet to thank. My second thanks to Sidney.
My first thanks to Sidney is for him to teach me traditional jazz, that's my first thanks and my second thanks is when he told Nichol Barclay,

"Take Chief. Take Chief, he'll impress you."
